newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P sees lower chance of quick Thomson-CSF sale.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees lower chance of quick Thomson-CSF sale.

text.p: Rating decisions about the debt of companies involved in the planned sale of Thomson-CSF reflect Standard & Poor's view that a quick sale of all or part of Thomson SA is "very much" reduced, S&P said on Tuesday.
"The outcome of the French parliamentary elections held on June 1st very much reduces the likelihood that the Thomson group would be partly or totally privatised short term," S&P said in a statement.
"Alcatel had applied for the majority of Thomson-CSF's stock. Standard & Poor's considers that this possibility no longer impacts Alcatel's creditworthiness," S&P said.

S&P's statements were the latest signs of growing doubt in French financial circles about whether the incoming Socialist-led government would proceed with privatisations planned by the outgoing conservative government.
The Socialists have not clearly stated their position on future privatisations since the election on Sunday.
S&P confirmed short term and long term debt ratings of Alcatel Alsthom, Thomson SA and Banque Arjil, in which Lagardere is the chief shareholder.
Alcatel and Lagardere have both bid to take over Thomson-CSF, the defence electronics wing of Thomson SA.

With regard to Thomson SA debt, S&P said: "The ratings had been placed on Creditwatch following the previous French government's 1996 announcement of its decision to privatise Thomson. The results of yesterday's election and the current majority's clearly-stated intentions to suspend the current privatisations in France sharply reduce the likelihood that Thomson SA or Thomson-CSF would be privatised short-term."
S&P made a similar statement about Arjil, which is controlled by the Lagardere family.
